messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident: VelvetHealth — funcall parser errors spiking in their VPC dedicated pool. Error rate 78% for tool/function calls, paging oncall.
Alex (oncall): Acknowledged, picking this up. Paging @Maria SRE and @Ben (eng-lead). Can someone paste the first error traces?
VelvetHealth SRE: Thanks Alex. We're seeing 500s when the model returns tool call payloads; parser throws "Unexpected token" during JSON parse. Started ~09:12 UTC, affects about 30% of requests in the last 5m, but hitting some important customer flows.
Maria SRE: I'm on the logs. Correlation looks like a new field `patientNotes` with unescaped newlines and occasional single backslash sequences. Parser library choked on that new shape after the last runtime rollout.
Alex (oncall): Impact: VelvetHealth production (VPC dedicated pool). Is this isolated to their tenant/pool? If not, page escalation.
Ben (eng-lead): Confirmed isolated. Only VelvetHealth's dedicated pool shows the regression. Other tenants unaffected. Good — we can do a tenant-specific mitigation.
Ryan (research): Likely schema drift: model output included raw text blocks and some malformed escapes. Parser v2 is stricter; v1 tolerated sloppy JSON. Quick check: sample payload:

```
{"tool":"send_event","args":{"patientId":"VH-2334","patientNotes":"Line1\nLine2\\"}}
```

The `\"` at the end is actually a truncated escape from the generator, causing parse failures.
Tina (ops): Rolling a quick mitigation: route VelvetHealth toolcall traffic to the legacy parser shim (v1) and disable the new parser in their routing policy. Command I will run:

```
redwoodctl routes set --tenant velvethealth --toolcall-parser legacy --force
```

This should be fast (no deploy), just routing config.
Alex (oncall): Do it, Tina. Notify customer SRE before change and mention brief failover window.
VelvetHealth SRE: Please do. We can accept brief failover; this is urgent for appointments flow.
Ops-Bot: Deploy request accepted: route change queued by Tina at 09:21 UTC. Change will apply to 6 workers.
Maria SRE: While routing flips, I'm going to patch the parser to tolerate stray backslashes and run a canary on a small fraction of traffic. Proposed quick fix (escape-cleanup shim):

```
def sanitize(s):
    # naive but fast
    return s.replace('\\\\"', '\\"').replace('\n', '\\n')
```

We'll run canary on 1% of VelvetHealth traffic to validate.
Ben (eng-lead): Prefer a config-only rollback to legacy parser first (Tina's route change). Then merge the escape-cleanup PR to staging and run canary. If canary passes, we can roll forward parser v2 with sanitizer.
Ryan (research): Also recommend adding a small model-side prompt fix to avoid emitting raw backslash sequences. I'll push a prompt tweak to VelvetHealth's model profile that prefers JSON-safe encoding.
Tina (ops): Route update applied at 09:23 UTC. Early metrics: error rate dropping from 78% -> 6% in 2 mins. VelvetHealth SRE, can you confirm customer side behavior?
VelvetHealth SRE: Confirmed — errors reduced significantly. Some in-flight failures persist but new requests look healthy. Thanks team.
Alex (oncall): Great. I'm going to start the incident timeline and severity: Sev2 (customer impacting, isolated). Notifying CS and account team.
Ops-Bot: Incident created: REDWOOD-INC-2026-1765432100. Pagerduty alert cleared for Albert (oncall) at 09:24 UTC.
Maria SRE: I'll open PR with the sanitize shim and mark it for expedited review. Once merged we'll run the 1% canary and monitor logs for malformed escape patterns.
Ben (eng-lead): Assigning follow-ups: (1) permanent parser robustness fix (owner: Ben), (2) model prompt safety change (owner: Ryan), (3) customer postmortem + timeline (owner: Alex). Please create Jira tickets.
Tina (ops): Can we add an automated regression test that injects malformed escapes into our eval harness for router safety? If yes, I'll add a card.
Ben (eng-lead): Yes — add to Redwood Optimize regression suite. Tag it high priority for the parser family.
Ryan (research): Canary started at 09:35 UTC on 1% traffic. Early logs show sanitized payloads parse fine. No downstream tool errors so far.
VelvetHealth SRE: We're approving the canary. Once stable, we prefer the permanent parser fix rolled into their pool during our low-traffic window.
Alex (oncall): For now, leaving VelvetHealth on legacy parser until we have parser v2 + sanitization validated. Estimated ETA for safe rollout: 6 hours. We'll update the customer and CS.
Maria SRE: PR merged at 09:48 UTC. Canary steady for 12 minutes, error rate at 0.5% for canary slice. Scheduling full rollout after 30m observation.
Tina (ops): Planned rollout at 10:30 UTC. Will perform incremental worker replacement with health checks. I'll post updates here.
Ops-Bot: Rollout started at 10:31 UTC on 8 workers. Replacements in progress.
Tina (ops): All workers healthy. VelvetHealth traffic now running parser v2 + sanitizer. Global error rate 0.4% (within baseline).
VelvetHealth SRE: Verified — flows back to normal. Thank you for quick coordination.
Alex (oncall): Closing active mitigation. Assigning postmortem owner (Alex). Please include timeline, root cause (model emitted truncated escape sequences => parser v2 strictness), mitigation, and preventive actions (eval tests, prompt guardrails, routing policies for quick tenant isolation).
Ben (eng-lead): Addendum: consider a feature flag for parser-strictness per-tenant to allow immediate softening in emergencies.
Maria SRE: Filed follow-up Jira tickets: RED-4231 (parser hardening), RED-4232 (eval harness case), RED-4233 (tenant parser feature-flag). Linking incident REDWOOD-INC-2026-1765432100.
Alex (oncall): Thanks all. I'll run the postmortem and ping support/CS with the incident summary.
VelvetHealth SRE: Appreciated. We'll do a joint postmortem on Monday. :thumbsup:
